questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

The availability of funds will be / ensured if they all tried to / submit the proposals on time.

options.text: The availability of funds will be
ensured if they all tried to

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**ensured if they all tried to**".

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the error lies in the part "ensured if they all tried to."
 
• **The use of the word "tried" is incorrect.**
 
• The given sentence is the passive form of the sentence in future tense.
 
 
• We use the formula of subject + will + be + past participle verb (ensured)
 
 
 
• The future conditional describes something that might happen in the future with a condition. 
 
• **In the given sentence, the availability of funds will be ensured in the future if in present the proposals are submitted on time.**
 
• **Thus, the use of the word "tried" should be replaced by the present form of the verb i.e. "try."**

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4.**

**Correct Sentence: ***The availability of funds will be **ensured if they all try to** submit the proposals on time.*

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. But she has no idea an aunt and uncle are waiting for her.

B. 'The Strange Child' is the story of a young girl who believes she is the only one on the planet.

C. Her parents simply vanished into thin air one day.

D. She travels the world in search of Nevada because she aspires to reside in the Mojave Desert.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**BCDA.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• On going through the given sentences, it is clear that the passage is about the subject and her belief.
 
• **Sentence B** introduces the story's main character and her belief that she is alone on the planet.
 
• **Sentence C **explains the reason for her belief - her parents disappeared.
 
• Further, **sentence D** reveals her goal of finding Nevada and living in the Mojave Desert.
 
• At the end the **sentence A** adds a twist to the story by revealing that she has relatives waiting for her, of which she is unaware.
 
• From the above explanation, it is clear that the correct order of the given sentences is **BCDA.**

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4**.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Did you not buy the return tickets to Dehradun?

options.text: Was the return tickets to Dehradun not bought by you?
Were the return tickets to Dehradun not being bought by you?
Had the return tickets to Dehradun not bought by you?
Were the return tickets to Dehradun not bought by you?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Were the return tickets to Dehradun not bought by you?**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in active form i.e. the action performed by the subject is expressed by the verb.
 
 
• Example: She(subject) wrote(verb) a letter(object).
 
 
 
• Now, we follow the following structure in case of active voice interrogative sentences that start with do/does/did:
 
 
• Active voice: Do/Does/Did + Doer + Noun/Pronoun + …… ?
 
• **Passive voice: Is/Am/Are/Was/Were + Noun/Pronoun + Preposition + Doer ……. ?**
 
 
 
• The sentence is in the interrogative form, so **we need to start with the helping verb "were" followed by the subject "the return tickets to Dehradun" and then the past participle of the main verb "bought".**
 
• **The object "you" becomes the agent of the passive voice and is introduced with the preposition "by".**
 
• **The negative form "not" stays in the same position as in the original sentence.**
 
• Thus, the sentence in passive voice would be: Were the return tickets to Dehradun not bought by you?

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4**.

questions.question:
Select the grammatically correct statement from among the given options.

A. It is a nice party. I am enjoying the party.

B. It is a party. I am enjoying an party.

C. It is party. I am enjoying a party.

D. It is the party. I am enjoying an party.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**It is a nice party. I am enjoying the party.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• We are asked to find out the correct statements among the given sentences.
 
• Now, let us understand the following points:
 
 
• **The correct sentence structure is "It is a [adjective] party" and not "It is party" or "It is the party".**
 
• The article "an" is used before words that start with a vowel sound, while "a" is used before words that start with a consonant sound.
 
 
• Therefore, "an party" in statement B and statement D is grammatically incorrect.
 
 
 
• In sentence C, the article "a" before the word "party" is missing.
 
 
 
• Thus, sentence A is grammatically correct as it follows the correct sentence structure and uses the correct article.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4**.
